note: These rules are learning design, not validation specifications or laboratory SOPs.

comprehensionChecks.prompt: The fictional treatment wells read lower than the vehicle controls. What would best strengthen this observation?

options.text: Read the same plate again on the luminescence reader
Repeat with independent biological preparations and add an orthogonal method, such as an imaging-based cell count
Add more wells filled from the same treatment preparation
Nothing more is needed; lower ATP-associated light already shows the cells died

comprehensionChecks.explanation: Independent biological repeats test whether the difference holds across separate preparations, and an orthogonal method checks that the change is not specific to the ATP/luciferase readout, for example a compound interfering with luciferase or cells holding less ATP each. Re-reading the plate or adding wells from the same preparation only describes repeatability within this one preparation.

comprehensionChecks.prompt: A treatment well has lower ATP-associated light than the vehicle wells. What can you safely say?

options.text: The treatment killed the cells
The treatment works by blocking ATP production
The fictional signal is lower; that could reflect fewer cells, less ATP per cell, or assay interference, so it is not proof of cell death
The treatment would work the same way in patients

comprehensionChecks.explanation: ATP-associated light is an indirect, viability-related signal. On its own it cannot separate fewer cells from less ATP per cell or from a compound that interferes with the assay, and it says nothing about mechanism or a real-world response.

comprehensionChecks.prompt: Why must the blank and vehicle wells be valid before a percentage of vehicle means anything?

options.text: They make the treatment signal larger
Blanks estimate the background and vehicle wells are the reference; if either is invalid, the percentage has no sound basis
They only matter for the handoff record
The percentage can be calculated from the treatment wells alone

comprehensionChecks.explanation: The calculation subtracts the mean blank signal and divides by the mean background-adjusted vehicle signal. A wrong blank shifts every value, and an invalid vehicle reference makes the denominator meaningless, which is why this trainer withholds the percentage when the controls fail.

comprehensionChecks.prompt: B5 and B6 were both filled from the same fictional treatment preparation. What are they?

options.text: Biological replicates: they show the difference holds across independent preparations
Technical replicates: they show how repeatable the measurement is within one preparation
Vehicle controls
Background wells

comprehensionChecks.explanation: Technical replicates are repeated wells from one preparation and describe repeatability. Biological replicates come from independent preparations, such as separate cultures or days, and test whether a result holds up. One cannot stand in for the other.

comprehensionChecks.prompt: You also want to look at intact, living cells under a microscope. Why would you set up separate matched wells?

options.text: There is no need; the same wells can be imaged as living cells after the ATP reading
The ATP assay breaks the cells open, so the measured wells no longer hold intact living cells
Matched wells are only needed for blank wells
To use up the remaining reagent

comprehensionChecks.explanation: In the lytic ATP assay family this trainer references, the reagent breaks the cells open to release ATP. A later live-cell observation needs its own matched wells, unless a qualified scientist has validated a compatible multiplex order.
